# Renewable Energy Dashboard Layout

A presentation-ready dashboard can show the three energy sources as separate trend panels, then a combined view to highlight the shift in the generation mix from 2020 to 2024.

## Chart Set for the Dashboard

### Chart 1: Solar Capacity Trend
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/sun.svg
- **Chart type:** Line chart
- **X-axis:** Year
- **Y-axis:** Capacity (GW)
- **Series:** Solar capacity
- **Caption:** Solar shows the fastest growth, rising sharply from 720 GW in 2020 to 1510 GW in 2024.

### Chart 2: Wind Capacity Trend
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/wind.svg
- **Chart type:** Line chart
- **X-axis:** Year
- **Y-axis:** Capacity (GW)
- **Series:** Wind capacity
- **Caption:** Wind grows steadily, increasing from 740 GW to 910 GW over the five-year period.

### Chart 3: Hydropower Capacity Trend
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
- **Chart type:** Line chart
- **X-axis:** Year
- **Y-axis:** Capacity (GW)
- **Series:** Hydropower capacity
- **Caption:** Hydropower remains the most stable source, with only slight gains from 1230 GW to 1255 GW.

### Chart 4: Renewable Capacity Mix
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/stack.svg
- **Chart type:** Stacked area chart
- **X-axis:** Year
- **Y-axis:** Capacity (GW)
- **Series:** Solar, Wind, Hydropower
- **Caption:** The stacked area chart shows total renewable capacity expanding mainly due to solar, while hydropower stays relatively flat.

## Key Insights from the Dataset

- **Solar is the growth leader:** It more than doubled over the period, making it the main driver of renewable expansion.
- **Wind is growing, but moderately:** The increase is consistent, but far slower than solar’s acceleration.
- **Hydropower is stable:** It contributes the largest base capacity, but changes very little year to year.
- **The renewable mix is shifting:** Total capacity growth is increasingly dominated by solar, which changes the balance across sources.

## Dashboard-Friendly Data for the Charts

- **Solar (GW):** 2020 720, 2021 845, 2022 1010, 2023 1260, 2024 1510
- **Wind (GW):** 2020 740, 2021 780, 2022 823, 2023 865, 2024 910
- **Hydropower (GW):** 2020 1230, 2021 1240, 2022 1248, 2023 1250, 2024 1255

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Build Slides] https://www.canva.com/templates/search/presentation/
Action: [Button: Make Chart] https://www.datawrapper.de/
Action: [Button: Plot in Sheets] https://www.google.com/sheets/about/

- Our World in Data energy data: https://ourworldindata.org/renewable-energy
- U.S. EIA electricity and renewables: https://www.eia.gov/energyexplained/renewable-sources/
